history.q: In which year was the United Arab Emirates founded as a federation?
history.fact: The union is celebrated every year on Eid Al Etihad, the UAE's National Day.

history.q: Who was the first President of the United Arab Emirates?
choices: Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum
Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan
Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Saqr bin Mohammed Al Qasimi
history.fact: Sheikh Zayed led the country from 1971 until his death in 2004 and is honoured as the 'Father of the Nation'.

history.q: Before oil, which industry was the economic backbone of coastal towns such as Dubai and Abu Dhabi?
history.fact: Divers wore a nose clip and held a stone weight to sink quickly to the oyster beds, spending months at sea each summer.

history.q: Which country announced in 1968 that it would withdraw its forces from the Gulf by 1971?
history.fact: The announcement prompted the rulers of the Trucial States, Bahrain and Qatar to begin talks on forming a union.

history.q: Before 1971, the emirates that formed the UAE were known collectively as what?
history.fact: The name came from truces signed with Britain, including the Perpetual Maritime Truce of 1853.

history.q: Which dynasty began ruling Dubai in 1833, when a branch of the Bani Yas settled at the Creek?
history.fact: Maktoum bin Butti led his followers from Abu Dhabi to Dubai in 1833 and became the first Al Maktoum ruler.

history.q: What is the traditional wooden sailing vessel used for pearling and trade along the Emirati coast?
history.fact: Dhows are still built by hand in yards such as Ajman's, and still carry cargo along Dubai Creek.

history.q: In which decade did Abu Dhabi begin exporting crude oil?
history.fact: The first cargo of Abu Dhabi crude was shipped from Das Island in 1962.

history.q: British sources of the early 1800s gave the coast of today's UAE which nickname?
history.fact: Some historians, including Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi in 'The Myth of Arab Piracy in the Gulf' (1986), dispute the label.

history.q: Which emirate joined the federation in February 1972, after the other six?
history.fact: Ras Al Khaimah joined on 10 February 1972, completing the seven-emirate union.

history.q: Before becoming Ruler of Abu Dhabi in 1966, Sheikh Zayed was the ruler's representative in which inland oasis region?
history.fact: Zayed governed the Al Ain area from 1946, where he became known for reviving the falaj water channels and planting trees.

history.q: Which Ruler of Dubai (1958-1990) became the first Vice President of the UAE?
choices: Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid Al Maktoum
Sheikh Saeed bin Maktoum Al Maktoum
Sheikh Hamdan bin Rashid Al Maktoum
Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum
history.fact: Sheikh Rashid drove Dubai's modernisation, backing projects such as Port Rashid, Jebel Ali Port and the Dubai World Trade Centre.

history.q: The Umm an-Nar culture, named after an island beside Abu Dhabi, flourished in which era?
history.fact: Umm an-Nar people (c. 2600-2000 BCE) built circular stone tombs and traded copper with Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley.

history.q: The renowned 15th-century navigator Ahmad ibn Majid came from Julfar, near which modern city?
history.fact: Ibn Majid wrote influential guides to sailing the Indian Ocean; Julfar was a busy medieval trading port.

history.q: In 1507, a fleet from which European power attacked the east-coast town of Khor Fakkan?
history.fact: The fleet was led by Afonso de Albuquerque, who went on to attack the strategic island of Hormuz.

history.q: Which two neighbouring states took part in union talks but chose separate independence in 1971?
history.fact: Talks began in 1968 among nine sheikhdoms; Bahrain and Qatar declared independence in August and September 1971.

history.q: Dubai's oldest existing building, which long housed the Dubai Museum, is which fort?
history.fact: Built of coral stone and gypsum in the late 18th century, Al Fahidi Fort guarded the landward approach to the town.

history.q: The Gulf's natural pearl trade collapsed in the 1930s because of the Great Depression and which other development?
choices: The opening of the Suez Canal
A British ban on pearl imports
history.fact: Kokichi Mikimoto's cultured pearls, perfected in Japan, made natural Gulf pearls far less profitable.

history.q: In 1932, which town gained the Trucial Coast's first airfield, a stop on Imperial Airways' route to India?
history.fact: Passengers stayed overnight at the Al Mahatta fort, which is now a museum of aviation.

history.q: What was the 1820 agreement between Britain and the sheikhs of the coast called?
history.fact: It was followed by the Perpetual Maritime Truce of 1853 and the Exclusive Agreement of 1892.

history.q: Remains of a Christian monastery from around the 7th-8th centuries CE were found in 1992 on which island?
history.fact: The monastery had a church and cells for monks; visitors to the island's wildlife reserve can see the excavated site.

history.q: The Battle of Dibba, fought on the UAE's east coast in the 630s CE, was part of which conflict?
history.fact: The battle followed the death of the Prophet Muhammad, when Caliph Abu Bakr's forces fought tribes that had broken away.

history.q: Whom did Sheikh Zayed succeed as Ruler of Abu Dhabi in 1966?
history.fact: Shakhbut, Zayed's elder brother, had ruled Abu Dhabi since 1928, through the collapse of pearling and the first oil exports.

history.q: Which British-officered force, raised in 1951, later formed a core of the UAE's armed forces?
history.fact: Renamed the Trucial Oman Scouts in 1956, the force passed to the new federation in 1971 as the Union Defence Force.

history.q: The large pre-Islamic port site of ed-Dur, which flourished around the 1st century CE, lies in which emirate?
history.fact: Finds at ed-Dur include Roman glass, Indian pottery and coins, showing trade links reaching across the ancient world.

technology.q: Which Dubai skyscraper became the world's tallest building when it opened in 2010?
technology.fact: Construction began in 2004, and the tower opened with a grand fireworks show on 4 January 2010.

technology.q: In 2014, Dubai International overtook London Heathrow as the world's busiest airport by which measure?
technology.fact: Its Terminal 3, built for Emirates, was among the largest buildings in the world by floor space when it opened in 2008.

technology.q: Palm Jumeirah in Dubai is a famous example of what kind of engineering?
choices: An artificial island built from dredged sand
technology.fact: Builders used about 94 million cubic metres of sand and 7 million tonnes of rock to create the island and its breakwater.

technology.q: In 2020, the Barakah plant made the UAE the first Arab country to operate what kind of power station?
technology.fact: Barakah's first unit began supplying the grid in August 2020, eight years after construction started.

technology.q: What was notable about the Dubai Metro when its first line opened in 2009?
choices: Its trains are powered by hydrogen
Its trains are pulled by cables
technology.fact: Guinness World Records once listed its Red Line as the world's longest driverless metro line.

technology.q: Masdar City in Abu Dhabi was planned as a showcase for what?
technology.fact: Its narrow, shaded streets and a wind tower inspired by traditional designs help keep pedestrians cool.

technology.q: Which oil producers' organisation did Abu Dhabi join in 1967?
technology.fact: Membership passed to the UAE after the federation was formed in 1971.

technology.q: Which technology supplies most of the UAE's drinking water?
technology.fact: The UAE also runs a cloud-seeding programme, flying aircraft that release salt flares into suitable clouds.

technology.q: Emirates, founded in Dubai in 1985, has operated the world's largest fleet of which double-deck airliner?
technology.fact: Emirates ordered more A380s than any other airline, and some of its jets offer on-board showers in first class.

technology.q: About how tall is the Burj Khalifa?
technology.fact: It has more than 160 storeys, and its observation decks rank among the highest in the world.

technology.q: From which country was the UAE's Hope Mars probe launched in July 2020?
technology.fact: It flew on a Japanese H-IIA rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center.

technology.q: A company from which country led the consortium that built the Barakah nuclear plant?
technology.fact: KEPCO's APR-1400 reactor design was chosen in 2009, and Barakah's four units were built one after another.

technology.q: What made KhalifaSat, launched in 2018, a milestone for the UAE?
choices: It was the first satellite to orbit Mars
It was the first Arab crewed spacecraft
It was the first satellite built entirely by Emirati engineers
It was the first satellite launched from UAE soil
technology.fact: The Earth-observation satellite was built at the Mohammed bin Rashid Space Centre in Dubai.

technology.q: Jebel Ali, opened near Dubai in 1979, is best known as what?
technology.fact: Often called the world's largest man-made harbour, Jebel Ali Port anchors a huge free zone of trading companies.

technology.q: In Al Ain's UNESCO-listed oases, what is a falaj?
technology.fact: Aflaj use gravity to carry groundwater to date-palm gardens, a technique used in the area for around 3,000 years.

technology.q: What was the purpose of the barjeel, a feature of traditional Emirati houses?
technology.fact: Open on four sides, the wind tower funnels moving air down into the room below; Dubai's Al Fahidi district has many examples.

technology.q: What is the main scientific goal of the UAE's Hope probe?
choices: Landing a rover near the Martian south pole
Returning Martian soil samples to Earth
Studying the Martian atmosphere and weather
Searching for water ice on the Moon
technology.fact: Its wide, high orbit lets it observe the whole planet's weather at different times of day across the Martian seasons.

technology.q: Which Dubai project, opened in 2016, extended Dubai Creek through to the sea?
technology.fact: The 3.2 km canal links Business Bay to the sea at Jumeirah, turning the heart of old Dubai into an island.

technology.q: Dubai's first oil exports, in 1969, came from which offshore field?
technology.fact: To store crude at sea, engineers built giant underwater tanks shaped like upturned funnels, known as Khazzans.

technology.q: Which giant solar plant at Sweihan in Abu Dhabi began commercial operation in 2019?
technology.fact: With about 3.2 million solar panels and around 1.2 GW of capacity, it was one of the world's largest single-site solar plants.

technology.q: Shams 1, which opened near Madinat Zayed in 2013, generates power using what?
technology.fact: Curved mirrors focus sunlight onto pipes carrying a heat-transfer fluid, which raises steam to drive turbines.

technology.q: Which US university's space physics lab partnered with the UAE to build the Hope Mars probe?
technology.fact: Emirati engineers worked alongside LASP scientists, with Arizona State and UC Berkeley also contributing to the instruments.

technology.q: Murban, a benchmark crude oil that gained its own futures contract in 2021, is produced in which emirate?
technology.fact: Murban is a light, low-sulphur crude produced onshore by ADNOC and traded on ICE Futures Abu Dhabi.

technology.q: The Burj Khalifa's three-lobed floor plan was inspired by which desert flower?
technology.fact: The tower's spiralling setbacks help 'confuse the wind', reducing the swirling forces that make tall buildings sway.

technology.q: When Etihad Rail's first freight line opened in 2016, what was it built to carry?
technology.fact: The 264 km line links the Shah and Habshan gas facilities to the port of Ruwais.

art.q: Which famous Paris museum lent its name to a museum that opened on Abu Dhabi's Saadiyat Island in 2017?
art.fact: Its vast latticed dome creates a dappled 'rain of light', evoking palm fronds shading an oasis.

art.q: Which white-marble landmark in Abu Dhabi, completed in 2007, is the largest mosque in the UAE?
art.fact: It has 82 domes and more than 1,000 columns, and Sheikh Zayed is buried in its grounds.

art.q: Dubai's Burj Al Arab hotel was designed to resemble what?
art.fact: Opened in 1999, it stands on its own artificial island about 280 m off Jumeirah Beach.

art.q: The façade of Dubai's Museum of the Future, opened in 2022, is covered in what?
art.fact: The calligraphy, by Emirati artist Mattar bin Lahej, spells out lines of poetry by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

art.q: In the UAE, Nabati is a much-loved traditional form of what?
art.fact: Composed in colloquial Arabic, Nabati verse has been written by Bedouin poets and by leaders including Sheikh Zayed.

art.q: Which plant-based dye is used for intricate hand designs before Emirati weddings and Eid?
art.fact: The bride's henna night, 'Laylat Al Henna', is a traditional part of Emirati wedding celebrations.

art.q: Which pear-shaped, short-necked stringed instrument is central to traditional Gulf music?
art.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for 'wood', and it is a distant ancestor of the European lute.

art.q: In which film does Tom Cruise climb the outside of Dubai's Burj Khalifa?
art.fact: Cruise performed the 2011 climb himself, secured by cables, on the world's tallest building.

art.q: Which film franchise shot scenes of the desert planet Jakku in Abu Dhabi's Liwa desert?
art.fact: Liwa's towering dunes stood in for Jakku in 'Star Wars: The Force Awakens' (2015).

art.q: Which architecture firm designed the Burj Khalifa?
art.fact: Lead architect Adrian Smith later designed Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia, intended to be even taller.

art.q: Which French architect designed the Louvre Abu Dhabi?
art.fact: Nouvel won the Pritzker Prize in 2008 and also designed the National Museum of Qatar in Doha.

art.q: Which emirate has hosted a major international art biennial since 1993?
art.fact: Sharjah was named Cultural Capital of the Arab World in 1998 and UNESCO World Book Capital in 2019.

art.q: Which architect designed the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi on Saadiyat Island?
art.fact: Gehry also designed the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, whose titanium curves made it a global icon in 1997.

art.q: Which 2021 Denis Villeneuve film used Abu Dhabi's Liwa desert to portray the planet Arrakis?
art.fact: The production returned to Abu Dhabi to film 'Dune: Part Two', released in 2024.

art.q: Dubai Opera, opened in 2016, has a shape inspired by what?
art.fact: Its 2,000-seat hall can be converted into a flat-floored space for banquets and exhibitions.

art.q: Abu Dhabi's oldest stone building, begun as a watchtower in the 18th century, is called what?
art.fact: Built to guard the island's freshwater well, it later became the ruling family's palace and seat of government.

art.q: Al Sadu, inscribed by UNESCO in 2011, is a traditional Bedouin form of what?
art.fact: Women weave Al Sadu on ground looms, using sheep, goat and camel hair in bold geometric patterns.

art.q: Al Ayyala, performed at weddings and national celebrations, is what?
choices: A performance with drums and bamboo canes
art.fact: Two rows of men face each other, swaying and chanting poetry to the beat of drums; UNESCO inscribed it in 2014.

art.q: Al Ain's Al Jahili Fort hosts a permanent exhibition of photographs by which British explorer?
art.fact: Thesiger twice crossed the Empty Quarter in the 1940s and described his journeys in 'Arabian Sands' (1959).

art.q: Which Emirati artist is widely regarded as the pioneer of conceptual art in the UAE?
art.fact: Hassan Sharif (1951-2016) turned everyday objects such as rope, cardboard and cutlery into art.

art.q: Roughly what is the diameter of the Louvre Abu Dhabi's great dome?
art.fact: The dome weighs about 7,500 tonnes, close to the Eiffel Tower, and is built from eight layers of star-shaped patterns.

art.q: Which curator became director of the Sharjah Biennial in 2003 and founded the Sharjah Art Foundation in 2009?
art.fact: She is the daughter of Sharjah's ruler, Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, himself a historian and playwright.

art.q: Which architect designed the falcon-inspired UAE Pavilion at Expo 2020 Dubai?
art.fact: Its 28 roof 'wings' can open and close, like a falcon spreading its feathers in flight.

art.q: Which British architect designed the Burj Al Arab?
art.fact: Working for the firm Atkins, Wright was asked for a building that would become a symbol of Dubai.

art.q: The vast hand-knotted carpet in Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque was made by about 1,200 weavers in which country?
art.fact: Covering about 5,600 square metres, it was woven in sections that were joined together inside the mosque.

politics.q: What is the capital of the United Arab Emirates?
politics.fact: The emirate of Abu Dhabi is also by far the largest, covering more than 80% of the country's land.

politics.q: How many emirates make up the United Arab Emirates?
politics.fact: They are Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah.

politics.q: Which family rules the emirate of Abu Dhabi?
politics.fact: The Al Nahyan belong to the Bani Yas tribal confederation, whose roots lie in the Liwa Oasis.

politics.q: By convention, the President of the UAE has been the ruler of which emirate?
politics.fact: Likewise, the Ruler of Dubai has traditionally served as Vice President and Prime Minister.

politics.q: On which date does the UAE celebrate its National Day?
politics.fact: It marks the declaration of the union in 1971 and is celebrated with fireworks, parades and flags across all seven emirates.

politics.q: Which regional bloc was founded at a summit in Abu Dhabi in 1981?
politics.fact: Its six members are the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman.

politics.q: Which world body did the UAE join on 9 December 1971, a week after its founding?
politics.fact: The UAE had joined the Arab League a few days earlier, on 6 December 1971.

politics.q: In 2006, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum became ruler of which emirate?
politics.fact: He succeeded his brother, Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid, and also became the UAE's Vice President and Prime Minister.

politics.q: What is the traditional Emirati council where rulers and elders receive people and discuss community affairs?
politics.fact: UNESCO lists the majlis as intangible heritage shared by several Arab countries, including the UAE.

politics.q: Which body, made up of the rulers of the seven emirates, is the UAE's highest constitutional authority?
politics.fact: Its members elect the President and Vice President from among themselves.

politics.q: How many members sit in the UAE's Federal National Council?
politics.fact: Half of the members are chosen by an electoral college, and the other half are appointed by the rulers of the emirates.

politics.q: Who succeeded Sheikh Zayed as President of the UAE in 2004?
choices: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum
Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi
politics.fact: Sheikh Khalifa served as president until his death in 2022; the Burj Khalifa was named in his honour.

politics.q: In 2017, the UAE became the first country to appoint a minister of state for what?
politics.fact: Omar Sultan Al Olama was 27 when he was appointed in October 2017.

politics.q: Which family rules both Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah?
politics.fact: The Qawasim were a major maritime power on the coast in the 18th and early 19th centuries.

politics.q: Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, a historian and prolific author, became ruler of which emirate in 1972?
politics.fact: He holds a PhD in history from the University of Exeter and has written many books and plays.

politics.q: Which Abu Dhabi presidential palace opened its doors to the public in 2019?
politics.fact: The working palace houses a library and exhibitions on Emirati governance, and hosts state visits and summits.

politics.q: For how long is a UAE President elected under the constitution?
politics.fact: Presidents may be re-elected; Sheikh Zayed was re-elected repeatedly and served from 1971 until 2004.

politics.q: In which emirate was the union declared in 1971, at the building now known as Union House?
politics.fact: The Etihad Museum, opened beside Union House in 2017, tells the story of the federation's founding.

politics.q: In which year was the UAE's provisional constitution of 1971 made permanent?
politics.fact: The same 1996 amendment confirmed Abu Dhabi as the permanent federal capital.

politics.q: Who was the UAE's first Prime Minister, serving from 1971 to 1979?
choices: Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum
Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid Al Maktoum
Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Hamdan bin Rashid Al Maktoum
politics.fact: His father, Sheikh Rashid, took over as Prime Minister in 1979; Maktoum returned to the post in 1990.

politics.q: In which year did the UAE hold its first elections for seats in the Federal National Council?
politics.fact: An electoral college chose half of the council's members; it was greatly enlarged for later votes in 2011, 2015 and 2019.

politics.q: Who became the first woman Speaker of the Federal National Council, in 2015?
politics.fact: She was also the first woman elected to the council, in 2006.

politics.q: Under the constitution, major decisions of the Federal Supreme Council need the votes of which two emirates?
choices: Abu Dhabi and Ras Al Khaimah
politics.fact: Such decisions need five of the seven rulers' votes, including both Abu Dhabi and Dubai, giving each an effective veto.

politics.q: Which family rules the emirate of Fujairah?
politics.fact: Britain recognised Fujairah as a separate Trucial State in 1952, the last to gain that status.

politics.q: Who became the UAE's first female cabinet minister in 2004?
politics.fact: She was appointed Minister of Economy and Planning and later served as Minister of State for Tolerance.

current-affairs.q: Which planet did the UAE's Hope probe reach in February 2021?
current-affairs.fact: Hope entered orbit on 9 February 2021, making the UAE the first Arab country to reach Mars.

current-affairs.q: Expo 2020 Dubai, delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, opened in which year?
current-affairs.fact: It ran from 1 October 2021 to 31 March 2022, the first World Expo held in the Middle East.

current-affairs.q: In September 2019, who became the first Emirati to travel to space?
current-affairs.fact: He spent eight days on the International Space Station and gave viewers a tour of it in Arabic.

current-affairs.q: Which UN climate summit did the UAE host in Dubai in late 2023?
current-affairs.fact: Its final text called on countries to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems, a first for a COP agreement.

current-affairs.q: Who was elected President of the UAE in May 2022?
choices: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum
Sheikh Khalid bin Mohamed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan
current-affairs.fact: The Federal Supreme Council elected him on 14 May 2022, the day after the death of his brother, Sheikh Khalifa.

current-affairs.q: In 2020, the UAE agreed to establish diplomatic relations with which country under the Abraham Accords?
current-affairs.fact: The accords were signed at the White House on 15 September 2020; Bahrain signed on the same day.

current-affairs.q: In February 2019, which pope made the first papal visit to the Arabian Peninsula, in Abu Dhabi?
current-affairs.fact: His open-air Mass in Abu Dhabi drew about 180,000 people, and he signed the 'Document on Human Fraternity' there.

current-affairs.q: From January 2022, the UAE government's official weekend moved to which days?
current-affairs.fact: The change aligned the working week more closely with global markets; Friday became a half working day for government staff.

current-affairs.q: In December 2021, the UAE celebrated which anniversary of its founding?
current-affairs.fact: The 'Year of the 50th' included the 'Principles of the 50', ten guidelines for the country's next half-century.

current-affairs.q: In April 2023, Sultan Al Neyadi became the first Arab astronaut to do what?
current-affairs.fact: His spacewalk lasted about seven hours, during a six-month stay on the International Space Station.

current-affairs.q: In April 2024, the UAE recorded its heaviest rainfall since record-keeping began in which year?
current-affairs.fact: About 255 mm fell in under 24 hours at Khatm Al Shakla near Al Ain, more than a typical year's rain.

current-affairs.q: In 2024, which UAE power station became fully operational when the last of its four reactors came online?
current-affairs.fact: At full output, Barakah can supply up to a quarter of the UAE's electricity.

current-affairs.q: The UAE's Rashid rover was lost in April 2023 when its lander crashed on the Moon. Which country's company built the lander?
current-affairs.fact: ispace's Hakuto-R lander lost contact during its final descent; the rover was named after Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed.

current-affairs.q: Who served as President of COP28 in 2023?
current-affairs.fact: Dr Sultan Al Jaber was also the UAE's Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology and chief executive of ADNOC.

current-affairs.q: In June 2023, the UAE introduced a federal corporate tax at what headline rate?
current-affairs.fact: It applies to business profits above AED 375,000; the UAE had introduced a 5% VAT in 2018.

current-affairs.q: Which group of major emerging economies did the UAE join in January 2024?
current-affairs.fact: Egypt, Ethiopia and Iran also joined BRICS at the start of 2024, alongside the UAE.

current-affairs.q: In October 2021, the UAE announced a target to reach net-zero emissions by which year?
current-affairs.fact: It was the first country in the Middle East and North Africa to announce a net-zero target.

current-affairs.q: In May 2025, which entertainment company announced plans for a theme park resort on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island?
current-affairs.fact: Announced with Abu Dhabi's Miral as Disney's seventh theme park resort, it would join Yas Island's Ferrari World and Warner Bros. World.

current-affairs.q: In 2023, the UAE's Hope probe made a close flyby of which Martian moon?
current-affairs.fact: Passing about 100 km from Deimos, Hope captured some of the most detailed images yet of the tiny moon's far side.

current-affairs.q: On COP28's opening day in 2023, delegates agreed to make which fund operational?
current-affairs.fact: The UAE pledged $100 million to the fund, which helps vulnerable countries recover from climate disasters.

current-affairs.q: Which spacecraft carried Hazza Al Mansouri to the International Space Station in 2019?
current-affairs.fact: It launched from Baikonur in Kazakhstan on 25 September 2019; he returned to Earth aboard Soyuz MS-12.

current-affairs.q: Sultan Al Neyadi flew to the International Space Station in March 2023 on which mission?
current-affairs.fact: He spent about six months in orbit, at the time the longest space mission by an Arab astronaut.

current-affairs.q: About how many visits did Expo 2020 Dubai record during its six-month run?
current-affairs.fact: After the Expo closed, the site reopened as Expo City Dubai, which went on to host COP28.

current-affairs.q: Who was named in 2021 as the first Emirati woman astronaut?
current-affairs.fact: She trained at NASA alongside Mohammad Al Mulla and graduated from its astronaut programme in 2024.

current-affairs.q: In March 2019, Abu Dhabi became the first city in the Middle East and North Africa to host which event?
current-affairs.fact: About 7,500 athletes from some 190 nations took part.

society.q: What rate of value-added tax has the UAE levied since it introduced VAT in 2018?
society.fact: VAT arrived on 1 January 2018 alongside Saudi Arabia's; the UAE had previously relied almost entirely on oil revenue and fees.

society.q: What is the name of the UAE's long-term residence visa for investors, professionals and talented people, launched in 2019?
society.fact: It lasts ten years and, unlike ordinary work visas, does not need a local employer as sponsor.

society.q: By 2023, the population of the UAE was closest to which figure?
society.fact: The population was under one million at the federation's founding in 1971; most growth has come from foreign workers.

society.q: The UAE dirham has been pegged at a fixed rate to which currency since 1997?
society.fact: The peg is 3.6725 dirhams to the dollar, so UAE interest rates generally track decisions of the US Federal Reserve.

society.q: In January 2023, Dubai suspended a 30% municipality tax on what?
society.fact: The fee for a personal alcohol licence was scrapped at the same time, in a move seen as supporting tourism and expatriate residents.

society.q: Which card do passengers use to pay fares on Dubai's metro, trams and buses?
society.fact: 'Nol' means 'fare' in Arabic; Abu Dhabi's buses use a separate Hafilat card.

society.q: Roughly what share of the UAE's residents are foreign nationals rather than Emirati citizens?
society.fact: Indians form the largest single community, and the UAE has one of the highest proportions of migrants of any country in the world.

society.q: As of 2024, what statutory national minimum wage did the UAE have for private-sector workers?
society.fact: The 2022 labour law allowed the cabinet to set one but it did not; employers must instead pay wages through the Wage Protection System.

society.q: In 2021, the UAE launched a one-year visa allowing people employed by companies abroad to live in the country while doing what?
society.fact: Applicants needed proof of a monthly income of at least 3,500 US dollars; Dubai had piloted a similar scheme in late 2020.

society.q: In January 2023, the UAE introduced a compulsory scheme giving private-sector and federal workers which protection?
society.fact: Workers pay as little as 5 dirhams a month and can claim 60% of their basic salary for up to three months if they lose their job.

society.q: What is the name of the federal programme launched in 2021 to boost the employment of Emiratis in the private sector?
society.fact: Nafis tops up Emiratis' private-sector salaries and pension contributions, and the scheme is backed by fines for firms that miss their quotas.

society.q: Under the labour law in force from February 2022, private-sector employees in the UAE had to move to which type of contract?
society.fact: Open-ended contracts were phased out; the same law formally recognised part-time, temporary and flexible work for the first time.

society.q: Which emirate moved its government employees to a four-day working week in January 2022?
society.fact: Sharjah's public staff work Monday to Thursday with a three-day weekend, going further than the federal four-and-a-half-day week.

society.q: Since the UAE deregulated fuel prices in 2015, how often does a government committee set the price of petrol?
society.fact: Prices track world oil markets; in mid-2022 petrol passed 4 dirhams a litre, a record for the country.

society.q: In November 2020, a package of legal reforms made it lawful for unmarried couples in the UAE to do what?
society.fact: The same reforms let non-Muslims drink alcohol without a licence and allowed expatriates to use their home countries' inheritance laws.

society.q: In 2023, which railway network was completed to link the UAE's emirates, initially carrying freight?
society.fact: The 900-km network runs from the Saudi border to Fujairah; a passenger service between Abu Dhabi and Dubai was promised for later in the decade.

society.q: In World Bank figures for 2021, the UAE ranked second in the world, behind only the United States, as a source of what?
society.fact: Migrant workers sent home around 47 billion US dollars that year, much of it to India, Pakistan, Egypt and the Philippines.

society.q: By 2023, the population of the emirate of Dubai was closest to which figure?
society.fact: Rapid post-pandemic inflows pushed rents up sharply in 2022 and 2023, making housing costs the main cost-of-living concern for residents.

society.q: Under UAE Emiratisation rules from 2022, firms with 50 or more staff must raise the Emirati share of skilled jobs by how much each year?
society.fact: The target is 10% by the end of 2026; companies that fall short pay a monthly fine for each Emirati not hired.

society.q: From 2022, buying property worth at least how many dirhams qualified an investor for a UAE Golden Visa?
society.fact: The 2022 reform also let buyers qualify with off-plan or mortgaged property, fuelling demand in Dubai's housing market.

society.q: From December 2019, the UAE applied a 50% excise tax to which products?
society.fact: Tobacco and energy drinks had faced a 100% excise since 2017; electronic cigarettes were added at 100% at the same time as sugary drinks.

society.q: From January 2025, employers in all seven emirates were required to provide what for private-sector workers?
society.fact: Abu Dhabi and Dubai had required it for years; the 2025 rule extended cover to the northern emirates with a basic package costing around 320 dirhams a year.

society.q: In 2020, the UAE became the first Arab country to give private-sector fathers paid parental leave of how many working days?
society.fact: The leave can be taken at any time in the six months after the birth; maternity leave for private-sector mothers was set at 60 days in 2022.

society.q: In 2019, a presidential directive required women to hold what share of seats in the UAE's Federal National Council?
society.fact: The rule applied from the October 2019 elections and put the council among the world's parliaments with the highest share of women.

society.q: In September 2022, which operator of Dubai's road-toll gates was floated on the Dubai Financial Market?
society.fact: The listing raised about 1 billion US dollars; the toll of 4 dirhams per gate had not changed since the system opened in 2007.

general.q: What is the currency of the United Arab Emirates?
general.fact: The dirham was introduced in 1973 and has been officially pegged to the US dollar at about 3.67 since 1997.

general.q: Which vast sand desert covers much of the southern UAE?
general.fact: The Empty Quarter is the largest continuous sand desert in the world, shared with Saudi Arabia, Oman and Yemen.

general.q: What are the traditional wooden water taxis that cross Dubai Creek called?
general.fact: A crossing between Deira and Bur Dubai takes only a few minutes and costs about one dirham.

general.q: Which bird of prey is a national symbol of the UAE?
general.fact: Abu Dhabi has a dedicated falcon hospital, and falcons can travel with their own passports.

general.q: Which animals race at tracks such as Al Marmoom in Dubai, ridden by remote-controlled robot jockeys?
general.fact: Trainers drive alongside the track, using remote controls to signal through the lightweight robot riders.

general.q: Which motorsport series races at Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina Circuit?
general.fact: The first Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, in 2009, began in daylight and finished under floodlights.

general.q: Which two countries share land borders with the UAE?
general.fact: Qatar lies close by across the water but shares no land border with the UAE.

general.q: What is the official language of the UAE?
general.fact: English is widely used in business, and Emirati Arabic is one of the Gulf dialects.

general.q: Abu Dhabi's Yas Island hosts a giant indoor theme park dedicated to which car brand?
general.fact: Its Formula Rossa roller coaster launches riders to 240 km/h in under five seconds.

general.q: Jebel Jais, home to a record-breaking zipline and some of the UAE's highest terrain, is in which emirate?
general.fact: Its Jais Flight zipline was certified in 2018 as the world's longest, at more than 2.8 km.

general.q: Which mountain range runs along the UAE's east, near the border with Oman?
general.fact: The range contains ophiolite: ancient ocean-floor rock that was pushed up onto land.

general.q: Which oasis city became the UAE's first UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011?
general.fact: The listing includes Hili's Bronze Age tombs, the Hafit beehive tombs and oases watered by falaj channels.

general.q: Which emirate's entire coastline faces the Gulf of Oman?
general.fact: Fujairah's port is one of the world's largest ship-refuelling hubs, lying outside the Strait of Hormuz.

general.q: Which is the smallest of the seven emirates by area?
general.fact: Ajman covers only about 260 square kilometres, less than 1% of the UAE's land.

general.q: Which slow-cooked dish of wheat and meat is a staple of Emirati Ramadan and festive tables?
general.fact: Wheat and meat are cooked for hours and beaten into a smooth, porridge-like dish, often in a clay pot.

general.q: Tal Moreeb, one of the world's tallest sand dunes, rises near which oasis?
general.fact: The dune rises about 300 m and hosts a hill-climb race for cars and motorbikes.

general.q: Which hardy desert tree is the national tree of the UAE?
general.fact: Its deep roots reach groundwater far below the sand, and it was the emblem of the UAE's 2019 Year of Tolerance.

general.q: The Dubai World Cup, one of the richest race days in the world, is held in which sport?
general.fact: It is run at Meydan Racecourse, whose grandstand stretches for more than a kilometre.

general.q: Nahwa, a village belonging to Sharjah, is unusual because it is surrounded by territory of which country?
general.fact: Nahwa lies inside Madha, an Omani exclave that is itself surrounded by UAE territory: a rare 'counter-enclave'.

general.q: The east-coast town of Khor Fakkan is part of which emirate?
general.fact: Thanks to Khor Fakkan and Kalba, Sharjah is the only emirate with coastlines on both the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

general.q: The UAE made its first FIFA World Cup appearance in 1990 in which host country?
general.fact: The team lost all three group games but scored twice, including a goal against West Germany.

general.q: Which club became the first Emirati winner of the AFC Champions League, in 2003?
general.fact: Al Ain won Asia's top club title again in 2024, beating Yokohama F. Marinos in the final.

general.q: Which mountain beside Al Ain is known for 5,000-year-old 'beehive' tombs on its slopes?
general.fact: A winding road climbs to near its summit and is a famous finish for the UAE Tour cycle race.

general.q: The Dubai Fountain was designed by the firm behind which famous Las Vegas water show?
choices: The Lake of Dreams at Wynn
general.fact: Its jets shoot water up to about 150 m into the air, choreographed to music beside the Burj Khalifa.

general.q: Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary, at the head of Dubai Creek, is famous for which birds?
general.fact: Bird hides let visitors watch thousands of waterbirds within sight of the city skyline.
